s1.syndrome_frame: Progressive visual impairment with night blindness and peripheral visual field defects
salient_findings: Night blindness since childhood
Inferonasal scotoma on Goldmann visual field
Abnormal electroretinogram with flat rod response
Hypofluorescence on fundus autofluorescence
Inner retinal thickening and disorganization on OCT
key_facts: Patient age 42
Symptoms present since childhood
No symptoms except night blindness
Visual acuity 20/25 to 20/30 in both eyes
Color vision normal
Few yellow spots on fundus examination
Indistinct grayish circle beyond the arcades
Inferonasal scotoma on Goldmann visual field
Abnormal electroretinogram
Fundus autofluorescence shows hypofluorescence
OCT shows inner retinal thickening and disorganization
Complete loss of photoreceptors in superotemporal region

shortlist.label: congenital stationary night blindness
shortlist.why_kept: patient has night blindness since childhood with normal color vision and specific fundus findings

shortlist.label: retinitis pigmentosa
shortlist.why_kept: patient has night blindness, inferonasal scotoma, and abnormal electroretinogram

shortlist.label: choroideremia
shortlist.why_kept: patient has night blindness, peripheral visual field defects, and specific OCT findings

shortlist.label: oguchi disease
shortlist.why_kept: patient has night blindness and specific fundus autofluorescence findings

shortlist.label: retinal dystrophy
shortlist.why_kept: patient has progressive visual impairment, night blindness, and specific OCT findings

raw.rationale: The patient's night blindness since childhood, abnormal electroretinogram, and fundus examination findings of few yellow spots and an indistinct grayish circle beyond the arcades are consistent with retinitis pigmentosa. The OCT findings of inner retinal thickening and disorganization, as well as the complete loss of photoreceptors in the superotemporal region, also support this diagnosis.

rejected.label: congenital stationary night blindness
rejected.why: Lack of progression and normal fundus examination would be expected

rejected.label: choroideremia
rejected.why: Typically affects males and has a more severe clinical course

rejected.label: oguchi disease
rejected.why: Characterized by a golden sheep-like appearance of the fundus, which is not present in this case

rejected.label: retinal dystrophy
rejected.why: A broader term that encompasses many conditions, including retinitis pigmentosa, but is not specific enough to explain the patient's symptoms and findings
